title: Zero Card Scenario – Main Menu
description: Validates 'no cards available' handling in main card menu including API response mapping, UI display, navigation, and regulatory-mandated error handling.
testDescription: As a user with no cards linked to my account, I access 'View Card Details' from the main menu. System should properly show the 'no cards available' state with mandatory regulatory text, boundary and navigation controls, and correct error mapping per API response codes.
prerequisites: User is logged in with no issued cards; API card details endpoint returns HttpStatusCode 204 or 203 with ID=31.
stepsToPerform: 1. Login to the banking portal. 2. Navigate to 'Cards' from the main menu. 3. Click on 'View Card Details'. 4. Await API response from card-channel/web-order/card-account/cards/details. 5. Verify response code is 204 or 203+ID=31. 6. Confirm UI displays 'No cards found' message as per regulatory wording. 7. Validate that recommended navigation buttons ('Order new card', 'Go to homepage') are visible and functioning. 8. Click 'Order new card' to ensure process launches. 9. Click 'Go to homepage' and validate redirection to home. 10. Validate audit log is recorded for this event.
expectedResult: UI presents correct 'no cards' state, regulatory text, functional navigation, and audit event. API-to-client mapping validated.
auditLogging: Audit event is generated for card view attempt and navigation actions
navigationOptions: Order new card, Go to homepage
dataMaskingValidated: No card PII in UI or logs

title: OTP Authentication – Attempts Exceeded Blocking
description: Verifies limit on OTP attempts, UI blocking, regulatory error dialog, audit, timer reset, and retry restriction as per regulation.
testDescription: As a user, I repeatedly enter incorrect OTP codes during card details authentication. The system must enforce regulatory blocking after the maximum allowed attempts, present the correct UI blockscreen wording, log the event, and prevent further actions for the defined timer window.
prerequisites: User has at least one eligible card, OTP send enabled, maximum attempts threshold is defined (e.g., 3).
stepsToPerform: 1. Login to banking portal. 2. Navigate to 'Cards' > 'View Card Details'. 3. Select a card and proceed through privacy enforcement screen. 4. Request OTP code via SMS. 5. Enter invalid OTP code. 6. Repeat step 5 up to maximum attempt limit. 7. Observe UI when limit is reached; blockscreen should appear. 8. Validate blockscreen has regulatory text and wait timer (e.g., 'Try again in X minutes'). 9. Attempt navigation or resend OTP and ensure blocked. 10. Confirm audit log and regulatory error mapping. 11. Wait timer and retry post window to ensure retry is allowed.
expectedResult: UI presents error blockscreen, retry restricted, audit event generated, accurate timer and regulatory text shown.
attemptCounterPersistence: Attempts persist across browser closes and navigation
auditLogging: Event for blocking, attempt count, and unblock

title: Full E2E Card Details View – Multi-Brand (Mastercard, VISA, AMEX)
description: Validates entire user journey from card selection, privacy screen, OTP authentication, card details view (with all brand-specific elements), copy-to-clipboard, timer, and completion. Covers API integration, UI branding, sensitive data masking, and audit.
testDescription: As a cardholder, I access card details for multiple brands – Mastercard, VISA, and AMEX – ensuring correct flow, UI differentiation, brand-specific logic (AMEX dual CVV), masked PII, single/multi card selection, timer logic, copy options, and full navigation including completion.
prerequisites: User has at least one Mastercard, one VISA, and one AMEX issued and eligible for card details viewing.
stepsToPerform: 1. Login to bank portal. 2. Navigate to 'View Card Details'. 3. View multi-card selection UI with proper branding and masking. 4. Choose Mastercard and proceed; complete privacy screen and OTP entry flow. 5. View details, confirm correct branding, card number, expiry, masked PII, and regulatory warning. 6. Attempt copy-to-clipboard while visible; confirm clipboard clearing after timer expiry. 7. Repeat with VISA card, validate similar process. 8. Repeat with AMEX, confirm dual CVV flow, UI differentiation, copy logic. 9. Wait for session timer to expire and check UI block. 10. Complete process using 'Finish' action. 11. Confirm complete audit trail for each step.
expectedResult: All flows complete with correct UI for each brand, timer and copy enforced, PII masked throughout, audit recorded, API responses mapped.
brandLogic: Mastercard, VISA, AMEX dual CVV, UI color/logo
clipboard: Copy allowed only when visible, cleared on expiry

title: Missing Phone – OTP Send Error and Recovery
description: Validates regulatory-mandated error dialog when no mobile phone exists, UI blocking, audit event, and return to main menu onboarding.
testDescription: As a user without any registered mobile phone, I attempt to authenticate for card details. System must show regulatory error popup, block further progress, log audit, and provide clear onboarding instructions for phone update/retry.
prerequisites: User has at least one eligible card but has no mobile phone on file; API returns HttpStatusCode 203+ID=31.
stepsToPerform: 1. Login to portal. 2. Go to 'Cards' > 'View Card Details'. 3. Select a card to view. 4. Complete privacy screen and trigger OTP send. 5. Receive API response indicating missing phone. 6. Observe error popup with regulatory wording ('No phone registered, update required'). 7. Attempt to proceed/close/error flows. 8. Ensure UI disables input and process cannot continue. 9. Validate navigation options ('Go to homepage', 'Contact banker'). 10. Confirm audit event for error occurrence.
expectedResult: Proper error dialog, UI block, audit event generated, onboarding options available for phone update.
regulatoryText: Popup matches regulatory language, phone masking
navigationOptions: Go to homepage, retry after phone update

title: Session Timer Expiry – Data Exposure and Completion
description: Ensures timer-based session control for card details exposure, enforced session end, UI messaging, clipboard clearing, audit, and navigation resilience.
testDescription: As a cardholder viewing card details, I leave the data visible until the 90-second timer expires. This should trigger session end, data masking, clipboard clearing, and UI blockscreen with regulatory text. Attempts to navigate or copy should fail, and audit logs must be recorded.
prerequisites: User with at least one eligible card and completed OTP authentication; timer countdown active on card details view.
stepsToPerform: 1. Login to banking portal. 2. Go to 'Cards' > 'View Card Details'. 3. Complete card and privacy screens, OTP entry. 4. View card details with timer count visible. 5. Attempt copy-to-clipboard and confirm success while timer active. 6. Wait until timer reaches zero; observe UI transition/block. 7. Verify card data is masked/hidden. 8. Check clipboard to confirm data is cleared. 9. Attempt to navigate or retry within expired session, confirm restricted. 10. Validate audit event for session expiry and completion.
expectedResult: Session ends at timer expiry, UI and clipboard cleared, navigation blocked, audit recorded.
navigationBlock: UI prevents return or retry until process restarted

title: Multi-Card Selection UI and Data Masking Validation
description: Ensures correct multi-card selection display, UI differentiation, PII masking, navigation, and caching for backwards navigation following issuance or in actions lobby.
testDescription: As a user with multiple eligible cards (e.g., Mastercard and VISA), I view the card selection UI, verify only cards linked to me are shown with masked data, select a card for details, and validate that cached cards allow seamless backwards navigation with proper privacy enforcement.
prerequisites: User with at least two issued cards (Mastercard, VISA), main menu or actions lobby flows accessible, valid API response with card list.
stepsToPerform: 1. Login to the banking portal. 2. Navigate to 'Cards' menu. 3. Click on 'View Card Details'. 4. Confirm multi-card selection UI appears with correct brand, product images, and last 4 digits masked. 5. Verify cards displayed are only those registered to user (no unauthorized cards or extra info). 6. Select one card (e.g., Mastercard) and proceed. 7. Click 'Back' to return to card selection, confirm card data is cached and correctly masked. 8. Select another card (e.g., VISA), verify repeat privacy enforcement, UI, and masking. 9. Use both 'Home' and 'Continue' buttons for navigation checks. 10. Validate audit log for card selection and navigation events.
expectedResult: Only user's cards appear, all PII masked, UI differentiates brands, cached data enables proper backwards navigation, audit trail generated.
piiMaskingLocations: Card list UI, backwards navigation, audit logs

title: Expired OTP Code Entry – Error Dialog and Retry Flow
description: Tests expired OTP scenario, regulatory error wording, UI block, retry functionality, audit logging, and session reset.
testDescription: As a user, I wait too long to enter the OTP code after it is sent, triggering an expired code validation. The system should show an error dialog with correct regulatory text, block further input, offer retry paths, and log the event for compliance.
prerequisites: User with eligible card, OTP code sent via SMS, timer expiry logic enabled.
stepsToPerform: 1. Login to the portal. 2. Navigate to 'View Card Details'. 3. Complete privacy screen and request an OTP code. 4. Wait until OTP code expiration time is exceeded (do not enter the code). 5. Enter the expired OTP code and proceed. 6. Observe error dialog with regulatory language ('OTP expired, start over'). 7. Confirm that code entry field is disabled/cleared. 8. Click retry option and repeat OTP flow; confirm new code sent. 9. Attempt navigation or resend old code, validate restriction. 10. Check audit log for expired OTP event and retry actions.
expectedResult: UI blocks expired code entry, regulatory error shown, retry initiates new session, audit log created.
regulatoryErrorText: Error dialog with OTP expiry language
retryDisabled: Session reset required for new OTP

title: OTP Code Format and Digit Boundary – Validation and Error Handling
description: Validates proper digit boundaries and input format for OTP code entry, error handling on under/over-length, UI and audit consistency.
testDescription: As a user, I try to enter OTP codes of various lengths and invalid formats (less than 6 digits, more than 6, alphanumeric input). System must enforce 6-digit numeric boundary, handle errors with proper dialogs, restrict entry and log failures.
prerequisites: User with eligible card, OTP authentication stage active, code input box visible.
stepsToPerform: 1. Login to the banking portal. 2. Proceed to card details view until OTP input stage. 3. Attempt to enter an OTP code with fewer than 6 digits. 4. Attempt to enter a code with more than 6 digits. 5. Enter an alphanumeric code (letters, symbols). 6. Attempt to proceed each time. 7. Validate UI displays error messages based on input format and boundary. 8. Check that code entry box restricts input or clears on error. 9. Attempt to resend code and repeat invalid input steps. 10. Audit logs capture failed attempt types and regulatory error mapping.
expectedResult: OTP input accepts only 6 numeric digits, all other formats rejected with correct error dialog and audit recorded.
errorDialog: UI displays distinct regulatory errors for short, long, and invalid codes

title: Manual Session End – Explicit Finish and Navigation Reversal
description: Ensures manual session end via 'Finish', UI and clipboard clearing, navigation resilience, audit events, and ability to restart session after explicit closure.
testDescription: As a cardholder viewing card details, I explicitly finish the session using the 'Finish' button before timer expiry. Card details and clipboard should be cleared, UI blocked, audit log generated, and functionality for retry/restart validated after explicit closure.
prerequisites: User with one eligible card, completed authentication; card details and copy functionality visible.
stepsToPerform: 1. Login to banking portal. 2. Navigate to 'Cards' > 'View Card Details'. 3. Select card and complete privacy/OTP flows. 4. View card details, verify timer and copy-to-clipboard options are active. 5. Click 'Finish' button prior to timer expiry. 6. Confirm UI transitions to session end screen, card details hidden, clipboard cleared. 7. Attempt to navigate back to card details screen, verify restriction. 8. Attempt to copy card data post-finish, confirm failure. 9. Use available buttons to return to cards main menu or retry flow. 10. Audit log records manual finish, completion, and attempted actions post-session end.
expectedResult: Manual finish clears data and clipboard, UI disables session, navigation and retry allowed only via restart, audit logged.

title: Brand-Specific UI and Dual CVV Display – AMEX Coverage
description: Validates special AMEX flow with dual CVV fields, brand-specific UI, regulatory texts, masking, timing, navigation, and audit events.
testDescription: As an AMEX cardholder, I view card details and CVV info, ensuring dual CVV display, correct UI branding, regulatory instructional text, timer enforcement, copy-to-clipboard controls, and masking. All navigation options and audit requirements must be checked for AMEX brand specialization.
prerequisites: User with valid AMEX card, eligibility for card details viewing, brandCode = 3 in API response.
stepsToPerform: 1. Login to banking portal. 2. Go to 'View Card Details', select AMEX card in card selection UI. 3. Complete privacy enforcement, OTP authentication. 4. View AMEX details screen, confirm dual CVV fields (front and back), correct brand logo, UI differentiation. 5. Validate regulatory text for AMEX (instructions for both CVV fields). 6. Click 'View CVV' to open CVV details, check text and data masking. 7. Use copy-to-clipboard and verify controls as per timer and visibility rules. 8. Wait for timer expiry, confirm session end and data removal. 9. Attempt navigation to main menu or explicit return options (back, finish). 10. Check audit logs for each action and session event.
expectedResult: AMEX UI shows dual CVV, correct regulatory text, data masking, timer control, navigation and audit compliance.
brandLogic: AMEX dual CVV flow, UI differentiation

title: Pre-View Privacy Enforcement Screen – Text, Navigation and Regulatory Compliance
description: Validates pre-view warning and privacy enforcement screen with regulatory text, images, navigation options, timer explanation, and audit event generation.
testDescription: As a cardholder about to view card details, I am presented with a privacy enforcement screen containing regulatory warnings, correct text, branded images, explanations about 90-second exposure, and clear navigation. This step must be validated for both main menu and post-issuance flows for regulatory compliance.
prerequisites: User is authenticated, has at least one eligible card, has selected a card for viewing; initial API call returned valid card data.
stepsToPerform: 1. Login to the banking portal. 2. Navigate to 'Cards' > 'View Card Details'. 3. Select a card from the multi-card selection UI. 4. Observe transition to the privacy enforcement screen. 5. Verify regulatory warning text ('No one else should view the screen', 'Do not store card info on phone or computer'). 6. Confirm display of branded card image, privacy icon, and explanatory tooltip. 7. Read timer information explaining 90-second exposure. 8. Check the 'Back' and 'View Card Details' navigation buttons. 9. Click 'Back' to verify return to selection screen with correct state. 10. Click 'View Card Details' to proceed; validate audit log for privacy enforcement event.
expectedResult: Correct privacy text, images, timer info, navigation, and audit log for privacy enforcement displayed to user.
regulatoryText: Privacy and confidentiality enforcement wording as per API text (cardConfirmationSecurityInfo, cardConfirmationPrivacyInfo, cardConfirmationTimerInfo)

title: OTP Resend Limit – Request Blocking and Timer Enforcement
description: Tests the boundary condition for OTP resend requests, enforcing regulatory maximum resend count, UI error popup, blockscreen, timer, and audit trail.
testDescription: As a user in the OTP authentication step, I repeatedly use 'Resend OTP' and 'Resend voice call OTP'. The system must enforce maximum resend boundary, present a regulatory-mandated error popup when limit exceeded, block further requests for defined timer window, and log audit events for each resend and block.
prerequisites: User is authenticated, eligible for card details, mobile phone present, at OTP entry stage; resend attempt count is tracked.
stepsToPerform: 1. Login and begin card details workflow. 2. Complete privacy screen and trigger OTP send. 3. Use 'Resend OTP' up to maximum allowed requests. 4. Attempt resend after boundary is crossed. 5. Repeat using 'Resend voice call OTP' if available. 6. Observe regulatory error popup on block event ('Too many requests, wait 10 minutes'). 7. Confirm blockscreen disables input and navigation. 8. Wait for timer to elapse, retry resend, check behavior. 9. Attempt to navigate away and return, validate block persists. 10. Confirm audit trail for resend attempts, block, and unblocking.
expectedResult: Regulatory popup shown for resend limit, input blocked for timer, audit logged for each request and block event.
resendBoundary: Boundary enforced for max resend attempts (SMS/voice)
attemptCounterPersistence: Attempt and resend counter persists across navigation/browser
auditLogging: Resend request, block, unblock events recorded

title: Unauthorized Card Data Access – API and UI Security
description: Verifies handling of unauthorized or foreign card access attempts, ensuring UI masking, regulatory error dialogs, navigation blocks, and audit logs.
testDescription: As a user who selects a card not registered to my identity, or attempts to access card details for a foreign/unauthorized card, the system must enforce strict UI masking, regulatory error dialog, block navigation to card details, and record an audit event for attempted unauthorized access.
prerequisites: User is authenticated, at card selection UI, card list includes unauthorized/foreign card through data setup or test injection.
stepsToPerform: 1. Login to the banking portal. 2. Navigate to 'View Card Details' > card selection screen. 3. Attempt to select a card that does not belong to user (data injected for test). 4. Observe UI masking: card info not displayed, card action buttons disabled. 5. System triggers regulatory error dialog explaining unauthorized access ('You may only view cards registered to your name'). 6. Try to proceed to privacy/OTP screen; confirm block. 7. Attempt to use navigation buttons ('Home', 'Continue'), ensure restricted. 8. Confirm audit event for unauthorized access attempt. 9. Repeat from different navigation entry points. 10. Check logs and UI for masking of PII fields.
expectedResult: Unauthorized access attempt results in masked card info, regulatory error dialog, blocked navigation, and audit event.
regulatoryText: Unauthorized access warning as per cardListDesc/cardListInfo
navigationBlock: No progression to privacy or OTP screens for unauthorized cards

title: Copy-to-Clipboard Functionality – Timer and Masking Compliance
description: Validates copy-to-clipboard option for card details, regulatory restrictions, masking, clipboard clearing at timer expiry or manual finish, and audit log enforcement.
testDescription: As a cardholder viewing card info, I use the copy-to-clipboard option for card number, expiry and CVV. The system must allow copy only when card info is visible, mask sensitive data in clipboard after timer or session end, clear clipboard immediately, and generate audit logs for copy actions.
prerequisites: User is authenticated, eligible for card details view, session timer active, card info displayed.
stepsToPerform: 1. Complete authentication and arrive at card details screen. 2. Click 'Copy-to-clipboard' button while card info is visible. 3. Confirm clipboard receives full card info for permitted view window. 4. Wait for 90-second timer to expire; verify clipboard is cleared immediately. 5. Click 'Finish' button before timer expiry; confirm clipboard is cleared. 6. Try to copy while UI is masked or session ended; confirm failure and regulatory warning. 7. Check audit log for copy action and clipboard clearing events. 8. Repeat test with AMEX dual CVV scenario and ensure both CVVs are managed. 9. Validate clipboard logic across web and mobile. 10. Attempt to retrieve clipboard content post masking, check for cleared state.
expectedResult: Copy allowed only when visible, clipboard cleared on timer/session close, regulatory warning, audit for copy and clear.
clipboardTiming: Copy permitted only during exposure window; immediate clearing at expiry
maskingLogic: Clipboard masked when card data hidden

title: Actions Lobby Post-Issuance Flow – Card Details and Retry Logic
description: Validates post-issuance card details workflow from actions lobby, handling card data not available, retry, regulatory text, navigation, and cache persistence.
testDescription: After ordering a new card, I access card details from the actions lobby. If card info is not yet available, system shows regulatory 'No card' state, allows retry after short interval or return to main menu, ensures proper caching for successful cases, and logs audit events. Workflow covers session transitions, cache logic, and retry controls.
prerequisites: User just completed card issuance flow, is at actions lobby; card info may be unavailable (API returns 203+ID=31).
stepsToPerform: 1. Complete card ordering process as normal user. 2. Arrive at actions lobby and click 'View Card Details'. 3. Await API response; ensure 203+ID=31 triggers 'No card found' screen with regulatory message ('Card not yet ready, try again soon'). 4. Use 'Retry' button, attempt retrieval again after short wait. 5. System retries API call and, if successful, transitions to card selection and privacy screen. 6. If not successful, allow navigation back to 'Home' and confirm correct redirection. 7. Confirm caching logic for successful retrieval (card data persists across retries and backwards navigation). 8. Validate audit logs for issuance, retry attempts, navigation, and successful view. 9. Check UI does not display new card PII until authorized. 10. Ensure retry interval is enforced and regulatory text matches requirements.
expectedResult: Post-issuance workflow handles unavailable card, retry logic, regulatory guidance, navigation, cache persistence, and audit logs correctly.
regulatoryText: No card found, retry guidance, main menu navigation
retryControl: Retry allowed after defined interval, regulatory text shown
cachePersistence: Card data cached after successful retrieval
auditLogging: Issuance, retry, navigation, successful view events recorded

title: Masked Mobile Number and PII Validation in OTP Screen
description: Ensures mobile number is masked in OTP authentication, all PII is masked in UI and audit logs, and privacy overlays are enforced consistently.
testDescription: As a user receiving OTP codes, I should see my mobile phone masked (e.g., 052-6***53), all personal data masked across UI and logs, ensuring privacy compliance. The scenario covers OTP generation, multiple brands, and regulatory overlays.
prerequisites: User with at least one eligible card, valid mobile phone number on file, OTP authentication stage active.
stepsToPerform: 1. Login to the banking portal. 2. Navigate to 'Cards' > 'View Card Details'. 3. Select a card and proceed to privacy screen. 4. Trigger OTP send; observe phone number masking on OTP screen (e.g., 052-6***53). 5. Validate UI does not display full phone number or other PII. 6. Enter OTP and proceed; check UI for further masking. 7. Review audit logs for any PII exposure. 8. Repeat process with AMEX, Mastercard, VISA to verify consistent masking. 9. Attempt navigation or resend OTPs; confirm masking persists. 10. Validate masking across web and mobile channels.
expectedResult: Mobile number is masked, all PII consistently masked in UI and logs, regulatory privacy overlays enforce compliance.
piiMaskingLocations: OTP screen, audit logs, navigation dialogs
auditLogging: Audit log contains masked fields only
brandLogic: Test masking for AMEX, Mastercard, VISA

title: State Transition Handling for Session Blocks and Retry
description: Validates persistence and correct state transition of session blocks due to timer expiry and OTP attempts, including retry logic after navigation or browser closure.
testDescription: Upon session block (from timer expiry or exceeded OTP attempts), the block should persist across navigation, browser closes, and explicit retries. Regulatory block wording and timer must apply, and retry should be permitted only after timer elapses.
prerequisites: User with eligible card, session block active from timer expiry or max OTP attempts, block timer running.
stepsToPerform: 1. Complete authentication and enter card details workflow. 2. Trigger session block by either timer expiry or exceeding OTP attempts. 3. Observe blockscreen with regulatory text and timer. 4. Close the browser and reopen the portal. 5. Attempt to resume card details workflow. 6. Check if block persists with same timer and regulatory text. 7. Attempt navigation within blocked session (back, home, retry); confirm block persists. 8. Wait for timer to expire; attempt retry after timer. 9. Validate session is reset and new workflow starts. 10. Check audit log for all block, retry, and unblock events.
expectedResult: Session block persists across navigation and closures; retry is enabled only after timer; audit logs for each transition.
attemptCounterPersistence: Block persists across browser and navigation
auditLogging: Block, unblock, and retry transitions recorded

title: Timer and Data Exposure – Edge Cases During Copy and Navigation
description: Tests copying card info immediately before timer expiry, rapid navigation actions, clipboard behavior on boundary, and regulatory timing.
testDescription: As a cardholder, I attempt to copy card info or navigate within 1 second of timer expiry. The system should enforce immediate masking, clipboard clearing, block navigation to details, and audit edge case timing accurately.
prerequisites: User with eligible card, session timer active, card details screen reached.
stepsToPerform: 1. Login and reach card details view with 90-second timer. 2. Attempt to copy card info at 89 seconds. 3. Try navigation to another card or back to privacy screen at 89.5 seconds. 4. Attempt to copy card info immediately before timer hits zero. 5. Let timer expire; watch UI transition and clipboard clearing. 6. Try navigation back to card details after expiry; confirm UI blocked. 7. Retrieve clipboard content post expiry; check for masking/clear state. 8. Repeat test across brands and channels. 9. Validate audit logs show precise timing and actions. 10. Confirm edge case handling for timer and data exposure boundaries.
expectedResult: Copy and navigation blocked at expiry, clipboard cleared, UI transition immediate, audit logs accurate for edge cases.
timerEdgeCases: Actions allowed only until expiry; immediate blocking at timer
auditLogging: Edge case timing and actions logged

title: Latency and Exposure Time for Card Details Retrieval
description: Verifies performance requirements for data retrieval, UI display, error response, and exposure window start/end. Ensures regulatory latency limits and audit event timestamps.
testDescription: On card details retrieval, system must meet latency SLAs: API response, UI rendering, regulatory warning display, timer countdown accuracy, and error dialogs. Audit timestamps for session start/end, copy, and error events are required.
prerequisites: User with eligible card, card details API, timer and copy logic enabled.
stepsToPerform: 1. Login and start card details workflow. 2. Select a card and observe latency for API call. 3. Record time from request to UI display of card info. 4. Validate timer countdown starts exactly at UI exposure. 5. Attempt copy-to-clipboard; measure latency for clipboard update. 6. Trigger an error (e.g., expired OTP); measure response time for error dialog. 7. Let session timer expire; check UI/block latency for transition. 8. Review audit logs for event timestamps: retrieval, copy, error, session end. 9. Compare all latencies against regulatory requirements. 10. Repeat across channels and brands for comparative analysis.
expectedResult: API response, UI rendering, timer, copy, and error dialog meet latency SLAs; audit event timestamps are accurate and traceable.
latencyMetrics: API, UI display, timer start/end, error dialog
regulatorySLAs: Latency must meet regulatory threshold (e.g., <1s UI, <2s API)

title: Comprehensive Audit Trail – Multi-Step Authentication and Card Access Events
description: Ensures complete audit event generation for each stage: card selection, privacy enforcement, OTP send/resend, validation, failure, session end, and all navigation across channels and brands.
testDescription: Throughout the card details workflow, every critical action and failure must trigger an audit event. This includes card selection, privacy screen, OTP actions, session transitions, copy, all navigation, and error/block screens. Events must include regulatory-mandated data, timestamp, masking, and result codes.
prerequisites: User performs card details workflow with audit logic active, integration with audit subsystem.
stepsToPerform: 1. Login and start workflow from main menu. 2. Select a card; check audit event for card selection. 3. View privacy enforcement screen; validate audit entry with regulatory data. 4. Trigger OTP send; audit for request and phone masking. 5. Enter OTP, succeed/fail; audit for validation result. 6. Resend OTP; audit for resend and limit enforcement. 7. View card details; audit for exposure and copy actions. 8. End session manually or timer; audit for session closure. 9. Trigger error/block screens; audit for every block reason and navigation event. 10. Review audit logs: all events have correct data, masking, timestamp, and regulatory result mapping.
expectedResult: Audit logs cover every critical step, data is masked, timestamps precise, meets regulatory mandates, traceable end-to-end.
auditEventCoverage: Selection, privacy, OTP send/resend, validation, card view, copy, session end, error/block screens, navigation
regulatoryCompliance: Meets audit mandates for financial services

title: Voice OTP Flow – UI, Masking, Resend, and Audit
description: Verifies complete voice call OTP workflow: selection, masking, resend limits, UI differences, regulatory texts, and audit across card brands.
testDescription: As a user eligible for card details view, I request OTP via voice call instead of SMS. The system should mask phone number, enforce resend boundaries, differentiate UI and regulatory text, handle failures, and record every step in audit logs. Repeat flow for multiple card brands (Mastercard, VISA, AMEX) and across web/mobile channels.
prerequisites: User logged in with at least one eligible card, valid phone number present, voice OTP request enabled, session active.
stepsToPerform: 1. Login to banking portal or mobile app. 2. Navigate to 'Cards' > 'View Card Details'. 3. Select a card and proceed past privacy screen. 4. On OTP screen, choose 'Send voice call OTP.' 5. Observe masked phone number (e.g., 052-6***53) and regulatory text specific for voice channel. 6. Enter received OTP and validate authentication. 7. Use 'Resend voice call OTP' up to regulatory max limit; observe UI popup on boundary. 8. Confirm error handling for failed call (API error, missed call). 9. Attempt navigation (back/home) during voice OTP session; validate state and audit logging. 10. Repeat for AMEX, Mastercard, VISA to check UI/wording differences and masking.
expectedResult: Voice call OTP flow operates correctly; UI, masking, resend limit, error handling, regulatory texts and audit logs accurate for all brands and channels.
voiceOtpEnabled: User can request and resend voice OTP per channel logic
phoneMasking: Consistent masking across UI and audit logs
brandUIText: Distinct regulatory texts for voice channel and for Mastercard, VISA, AMEX
auditLogging: Audit for each OTP send/resend, entry, error and navigation
errorHandling: Voice-specific failures (missed call, API errors) handled with regulatory popup

title: Card Details API Error Codes – Decision Table Exhaustion
description: Covers full API status/ID code matrix for card details retrieval, ensuring correct UI, masking, navigation and regulatory error responses.
testDescription: On retrieving card details via API, system must handle all response code combinations: 203+ID=31, 203+ID=32, 204, 400, 500, and other edge codes. Each must map to a regulatory error screen or UI message, ensuring no PII exposure, correct masking, navigation controls, and proper audit logging. Decision table testing covers full matrix as per regulatory mandates.
prerequisites: User authenticated, eligible for card details (test harness can inject any API response code).
stepsToPerform: 1. Login to cards portal. 2. Initiate 'View Card Details' workflow. 3. Simulate API returning 203+ID=31; observe 'no card' regulatory screen. 4. Simulate API returning 204; confirm similar regulatory error and navigation buttons. 5. Simulate API error responses (400, 500); observe generic/technical error screen with regulatory guidance and masking. 6. Simulate API with 203+ID=32; confirm blockscreen and error text for exceeded attempts. 7. Validate UI does not expose sensitive card info for any failure. 8. Try navigation (home, retry, back) for each code; check state handling and audit logs. 9. Review audit log for error event, regulatory mapping. 10. Compare UI and error mapping for all codes against business/regulatory tables.
expectedResult: All API codes mapped to correct regulatory UI/error, masking enforced, navigation resilient, audit logs recorded, no sensitive info exposed.
decisionTableCoverage: Each API outcome mapped to UI/error per regulatory table
maskingLogic: PII never exposed in error flows

title: Mobile Channel Integration – Card View, Authentication, and Responsive UI
description: Validates full card details viewing workflow in mobile app: responsive UI, authentication, timer logic, copy controls, masking, navigation, audit and regulatory overlays for all brands.
testDescription: As a mobile user, I start from the card actions lobby, select a card, pass through privacy screen, complete OTP authentication, view masked/unmasked card data, use timer/copy, navigate through session end, and attempt backward navigation post-session. The scenario exhaustively validates responsive UI elements, regulatory texts, masking of PII, copy-to-clipboard logic, timer exposure, mobile-specific behaviors, error screens, and audit tracking for Mastercard, VISA, AMEX, Isracard.
prerequisites: Mobile app installed, user authenticated, eligible cards issued (all major brands), actions lobby enabled.
stepsToPerform: 1. Launch mobile app and login. 2. Navigate to card actions lobby. 3. Select 'View Card Details' for eligible card (Mastercard). 4. Complete privacy enforcement screen; verify responsive layout and regulatory text. 5. Request OTP and enter code; confirm input and masking, timer presentation. 6. Observe card details screen: card number, expiry, CVV, brand logo. 7. Use copy-to-clipboard for card number and CVV; verify permitted only when visible. 8. Let session timer run to expiry; confirm UI blocks and clipboard clears. 9. Attempt navigation back to card selection and privacy screen; check cache/masking. 10. Repeat flow for VISA, AMEX, Isracard; verify brand-specific UI, dual CVV, regulatory overlays. 11. Check audit logs for every mobile event: card selection, authentication, copy, session end.
expectedResult: Mobile channel shows all UI correctly, responsive design, timer logic, copy-to-clipboard, masking, error and regulatory overlays; audit logs complete for all actions and brands.
brandLogic: Mastercard, VISA, AMEX dual CVV, Isracard
responsiveUI: UI adapts for mobile screen, touch controls
navigationBehavior: Backwards navigation handled per regulatory guidelines

title: Invalid Authentication – Birthdate and Name Mismatch Handling
description: Tests user entry of mismatched birthdate or name during authentication, ensures regulatory error dialogs, masking, navigation blocks, and audit compliance.
testDescription: During card details authentication, user enters an incorrect birthdate or mismatched name (as required for some flows or brands). System must intercept, show a regulatory error popup, mask any personal info, restrict further input/navigation, and record audit event for the failed authentication attempt. Flows must prevent any unauthorized access and offer guidance for retry.
prerequisites: User authenticated, at OTP authentication stage, input fields for birthdate/name enabled where required by brand or workflow.
stepsToPerform: 1. Login to the banking portal. 2. Go to 'View Card Details' and select a card. 3. Proceed to privacy enforcement and authentication. 4. Enter an incorrect birthdate or mismatched name. 5. Attempt OTP send/validation. 6. Observe UI error dialog with regulatory text ('Authentication failed, please verify your details'). 7. Confirm all input fields are masked and no sensitive info exposed. 8. Try navigation (home, retry, back) after error; confirm all actions are blocked. 9. Follow regulatory guidance provided in error screen for retry/onboarding. 10. Validate audit log records failed authentication and attempted navigation.
expectedResult: Incorrect birthdate/name triggers regulatory error dialog, input masking, navigation block, retry guidance, and audit event without PII exposure.
navigationBlock: No progression until correct details provided
auditLogging: Failed authentication attempt and actions logged

title: Session Timeout and API Failover – Resilience and Recovery
description: Validates functional and performance resilience for session timeout and API failover during card details workflow; ensures recovery actions, regulatory UI, audit, and masking.
testDescription: As a user viewing card details, I experience session timeout or API failover (network/API outage, slow response). System must block UI, show regulatory message, clear sensitive data and clipboard, log audit event, and provide recovery actions (retry or return to main menu) once service is restored. Performance is measured for failover handling, error dialog latency, and recovery.
prerequisites: User authenticated, at card details view, session timer or API failover logic enabled, clipboard active.
stepsToPerform: 1. Login to cards portal and begin card details workflow. 2. Select card and view details after OTP authentication. 3. Simulate session timeout or API failure (network/API outage, artificial delay). 4. Wait for UI to detect failover/timeout; verify regulatory error screen is displayed immediately. 5. Check card details and clipboard are cleared without delay. 6. Attempt navigation (back, home, retry); confirm system only allows permitted options (return to main menu or retry per regulatory rules). 7. Restore API/network; attempt retry and check recovery to card details process. 8. Measure latency of failover detection and UI error display. 9. Validate masking of PII in all error screens and logs. 10. Review audit log for timeout/failover event, clipboard clearing, navigation, and recovery.
expectedResult: Session timeout or API failover triggers immediate regulatory error UI, sensitive data/clipboard cleared, navigation and recovery restricted, audit logs accurate, latency within SLA.
recoveryOptions: Return to main menu or retry only after service restoration
maskingLogic: PII masked in all error/failover screens

title: Card Selection State Transition – Cache and Return Post-Session
description: Verifies state persistence and cache usage for card details after session completion (timer/manual), including back navigation, selection UI, masking, and regulatory text.
testDescription: As a user who has finished a card details session (timer expiry or manual), I attempt to return to the card selection UI. The system should show correct masking, recall last selected card and details state, enforce privacy overlays, and ensure regulatory text guidance for session resumption.
prerequisites: User has completed card details session for one card (timer/manual), multi-card selection UI available; cache enabled.
stepsToPerform: 1. Login to the card portal as a user with multiple eligible cards. 2. Navigate to 'View Card Details' and select a card. 3. Complete privacy enforcement and OTP authentication. 4. View card details and allow session to expire or manually click 'Finish.' 5. Observe transition to session end screen with regulatory text. 6. Click 'Back' or equivalent navigation to return to card selection UI. 7. Verify previously selected card appears with details masked and privacy overlays active. 8. Attempt to select another card; repeat privacy/OTP flow. 9. Confirm audit event for back navigation, selection state, and session end. 10. Check cache does not retain sensitive data from expired session.
expectedResult: Card selection UI recalls last card, masking and privacy overlays enforced, regulatory text displayed, cache does not expose expired card details, audit logs include navigation and session transition.
cachePersistence: Session/cached state retained for non-PII only, previous card masked
piiMaskingLocations: Card selection UI post-session, cache, audit logs
navigationOptions: Back, select new card, session restart
auditLogging: Session end, back navigation, card re-selection

title: Card Details Exposure – Multiple Brand CVV Conditional Display
description: Tests brand-dependent CVV display permutations: single CVV, dual CVV, conditional UI for AMEX, Isracard, Mastercard, VISA, and regulatory masking for each.
testDescription: As a user viewing card details for different brands, I validate CVV presentation logic: AMEX shows both front and back CVVs, others display only one, Isracard may mask or conditionally display the CVV. Workflow ensures UI differentiation, error handling, masking, and audit for each variant.
prerequisites: User issued cards of at least three brands (AMEX, VISA, Isracard, Mastercard), CVV conditional flow enabled.
stepsToPerform: 1. Login to banking portal. 2. Navigate to 'View Card Details,' select Mastercard from the selection UI. 3. Complete privacy enforcement and OTP authentication. 4. View card details; confirm single CVV display and masking. 5. Repeat steps 2–4 for VISA and Isracard; check CVV display matches brand logic. 6. Select AMEX card; confirm dual CVV fields, regulatory instructions, masking. 7. Attempt navigation to CVV screen for each card; observe conditional UI and regulatory overlays. 8. Try copy-to-clipboard actions for each CVV permutation; validate permission and masking rules. 9. Wait for timer expiry and check CVV masking. 10. Audit actions for all brand flows and CVV accesses.
expectedResult: Brand logic respected for CVV display, masking enforced, UI correct for each permutation, conditional permissions applied, audit logs complete.
brandLogic: AMEX dual CVV, Isracard conditional, Mastercard/VISA single CVV
cvvPermissions: Copy/mask allowed only per regulatory logic

title: Failed Card Details Retrieval – API Timeout and UI Recovery
description: Validates UI and backend handling of API timeout during card details retrieval, ensuring regulatory error dialog, masking, navigation recovery/up-options, and audit.
testDescription: As a user attempting to retrieve card details when the backend API times out, I am shown a regulatory-compliant error dialog. Sensitive info is masked, navigation to retry or home is offered, session is not initiated, and audit logs are made for the failure and attempted actions.
prerequisites: User eligible for card details, API timeout simulated on retrieval endpoint, timer/session not started.
stepsToPerform: 1. Login to cards portal. 2. Navigate to 'View Card Details.' 3. Select card from UI. 4. System attempts card details API call and times out. 5. Observe UI transition to regulatory error dialog with timeout wording. 6. Confirm no card data is visible or cached. 7. Check available recovery navigation options: 'Retry,' 'Go to homepage.' 8. Attempt retry and confirm API call re-attempt logic. 9. Try to access card details UI directly; confirm masking persists. 10. Review audit logs for retrieval timeout, error, navigation, and retry actions.
expectedResult: Timeout triggers regulatory error dialog, all PII masked, navigation recovery available, session not initiated, audit logs for all actions.
errorHandling: Timeout mapping to regulatory error screen, no PII exposure
maskingLogic: UI and logs masked, cache cleared

title: Explicit Navigation Return from Card Details View – Session State and Audit
description: Verifies explicit return from card details or CVV view to card main menu, session closure, masking, UI state, regulatory guidance, and audit enforcement.
testDescription: As a cardholder viewing card details or CVV info, I use available navigation ('Return to main menu' or 'Back to card selection') to exit the details view before timer expiry. System must mask card data, close session, present regulatory guidance, and log audit events for navigation, closure, and session transitions.
prerequisites: User authenticated, card details or CVV screen active, session timer running, navigation controls visible.
stepsToPerform: 1. Login and advance to card details view following privacy/OTP flow. 2. Observe active timer and card/CVV data. 3. Click 'Return to main menu' button. 4. Check transition to card main menu UI, card details masked. 5. Attempt navigation back to card details view; verify session is closed and UI remains masked. 6. Try to access CVV or re-copy card info; confirm failure and regulatory guidance. 7. Confirm explicit regulatory text is present on return screen. 8. Attempt 'Back to card selection' navigation; validate UI and masking. 9. Check audit log includes navigation, session closure, and masking actions. 10. Validate cache does not retain exposed card data post-navigation.
expectedResult: Explicit navigation returns user to card main menu, session closed, card data masked, regulatory messages shown, audit trail correct.
navigationOptions: Return to main menu, Back to card selection

title: Card Details Input Validation – Leading/Trailing Whitespace and Invalid Characters
description: Tests input field validation for OTP, card suffix, and birthdate during authentication, ensuring error handling for whitespace, invalid characters, UI feedback, and audit logging.
testDescription: As a user entering credentials for card details authentication, I accidentally input leading/trailing spaces, symbols, or non-numeric characters into OTP, card suffix, or birthdate fields. System must reject invalid formats with regulatory error dialogs, clear input fields, block navigation, and record audit events.
prerequisites: User authenticated, at OTP/card/birthdate input stage, input validation logic active.
stepsToPerform: 1. Login and start authentication flow for card details. 2. Enter OTP code with leading whitespace and attempt to proceed. 3. Enter card suffix or birthdate with trailing spaces; try progression. 4. Input symbols or non-numeric characters into OTP/card fields. 5. System displays regulatory error dialog for each invalid input. 6. Input fields are cleared and made active for new input. 7. Navigation options ('Back,' 'Continue') are blocked until valid input provided. 8. Retry with valid input; confirm successful progression. 9. Review audit logs for invalid input attempts and error mappings. 10. Validate input logic for all brands and channels.
expectedResult: Invalid input triggers regulatory error dialog, input fields cleared, navigation blocked, audit logged; only valid numeric input permitted.
errorDialog: Distinct regulatory dialogs for each invalid input type
